paragraphs: On February 10, 2021, (the "Closing Date"), Nuvation Bio Inc., a Delaware corporation ("Legacy Nuvation Bio"), Panacea Acquisition Corp. ("Panacea"), and Panacea Merger Subsidiary Corp, a Delaware corporation and a direct, wholly owned subsidiary of Panacea ("Merger Sub") consummated the transactions contemplated by an Agreement and Plan of Merger among them dated October 20, 2020 ("Merger Agreement").

Pursuant to the terms of the Merger Agreement, a business combination of Panacea and Legacy Nuvation Bio was effected through the merger of Merger Sub with and into Legacy Nuvation Bio, with Legacy Nuvation Bio surviving as a wholly owned subsidiary of Panacea (the "Merger"). On the Closing Date, Legacy Nuvation Bio changed its name to Nuvation Bio Operating Company Inc. and Panacea changed its name to Nuvation Bio Inc. (the "Company" or "Nuvation Bio").

In connection with the closing of the Merger, our Class A common stock and warrants to purchase shares of our Class A common stock began trading on The New York Stock Exchange under the symbols "NUVB" and "NUVB.WS," respectively, on February 11, 2021. The disclosure in Items 1 and 1A of this report gives effect to the Merger and includes the operations of Legacy Nuvation Bio prior to the Merger.

On April 9, 2024 (the "Acquisition Date"), the Company completed its acquisition of AnHeart Therapeutics Ltd., an exempted company incorporated under the laws of the Cayman Islands ("AnHeart"), pursuant to that certain Agreement and Plan of Merger (the "AnHeart Merger Agreement"), by and among the Company, AnHeart, Artemis Merger Sub I, Ltd., an exempted company incorporated under the laws of the Cayman Islands and a wholly owned
subsidiary of the Company, and Artemis Merger Sub II, Ltd., an exempted company incorporated under the laws of the Cayman Islands and a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company.

"Nuvation Bio" is a registered trademark of Nuvation Bio Inc. in the U.S. and other countries. Other trademarks or service marks appearing in this report may be trademarks or service marks of other owners.

We are a global oncology company focused on tackling some of the toughest challenges in cancer treatment with the goal of developing therapies that create a profound, positive impact on patients' lives. We were founded in 2018 by our chief executive officer, David Hung, M.D., who founded Medivation, Inc. and led its successful development of oncology drugs Xtandi® and talazoparib (now marketed as Talzenna®), leading to its $14.3 billion sale to Pfizer Inc. ("Pfizer") in 2016.

We leverage our team's extensive expertise in medicinal chemistry, preclinical development, drug development, business development, manufacturing, and commercialization to pursue oncology targets validated by strong clinical or preclinical data and develop novel small molecules that improve the activity and overcome the liabilities of currently marketed drugs.

• The pursuit of validated targets: We identify and pursue oncology targets validated by strong clinical or preclinical data that provide a high degree of confidence in generating clinically meaningful benefit. We focus on targets where there has been some progress by others in generating clinical candidates or approved drugs, and we then attempt to design or acquire novel or potential best-in-class product candidates to overcome the encountered safety liabilities or limitations in efficacy.

• Innovative medicinal chemistry expertise: We use our medicinal chemistry proficiency to generate differentiated product candidates, focused on improving their safety, anti-tumor activity and pharmacologic profiles over other standard of care ("SOC") therapies. We also use innovative medicinal chemistry approaches to generate novel classes of molecules such as our drug-drug-conjugates ("DDCs").

• Human capital management: We believe our employees are our greatest assets. Attracting, motivating and retaining talent at all levels is vital to our continued success. We are building a culture that fosters a productive, professional and inclusive work environment, where people can thrive, have fun, and be inspired to perform their best work.

We commercially launched IBTROZI in the U.S. in June 2025, following its approval by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration ("FDA") on June 11, 2025 for the treatment of adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic ROS1-positive ("ROS1+") non-small cell lung cancer ("NSCLC"). Taletrectinib has also been approved by Japan's Ministry of Health, Labour, and Welfare ("MHLW") and by China's National Medical Products Administration ("NMPA") for the treatment of adult patients with ROS1+ locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC ("mNSCLC"). Taletrectinib is being commercialized in Japan by our partner Nippon Kayaku Co., Ltd ("NK") under the brand name IBTROZI and in China by our partner Innovent Biologics (Suzhou) Co. Ltd. ("Innovent") under the brand name DOVBLERON®. Taletrectinib has been granted Orphan Drug Designation by the U.S. FDA for the treatment of patients with ROS1+ NSCLC and other NSCLC indications and was previously granted Breakthrough Therapy Designations by both the U.S. FDA and China's NMPA for the treatment of patients with locally advanced or metastatic ROS1+ NSCLC. In January 2026, we announced a partnership with Eisai Co., Ltd. ("Eisai") to commercialize taletrectinib in Europe and other territories outside the U.S., China and Japan. In partnership with Eisai, we expect to submit a Marketing Authorization Application ("MAA") to the European Medicines Agency ("EMA") in the first half of 2026.

Taletrectinib continues to be evaluated for the treatment of patients with locally advanced or metastatic ROS1+ NSCLC in two Phase 2 single-arm pivotal studies: TRUST-I in China, and TRUST-II, a global study, as well as in a confirmatory randomized Phase 3 study versus crizotinib in China known as TRUST-III. In September 2025, we announced our first patient was enrolled in a global Phase 3, placebo-controlled study known as TRUST-IV, to evaluate taletrectinib for the adjuvant treatment of patients with resected ROS1+ early-stage NSCLC.

paragraphs: Our business and investing in our securities involve significant risks, some of which are described below. Before you make a decision to buy our securities, in addition to the risks and uncertainties discussed in the section titled "Cautionary Information Regarding Forward-Looking Statements," you should carefully consider the risks and uncertainties described below together with all of the other information contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including our financial statements and related notes and in the section titled "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations." The occurrence of any of the events or developments described in the following risk factors and the risks described elsewhere in this report could harm our business, financial condition, results of operations, cash flows, the trading price of our common stock and our growth prospects. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial may also impair our business operations. This report on Form 10-K also contains forward-looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties. Our actual results could differ materially from those anticipated in the forward-looking statements as a result of factors that are described in the following risk factors and the risks described elsewhere in this report.

Our near-term prospects are significantly dependent on the commercialization of IBTROZI. If we are unable to successfully commercialize IBTROZI, our ability to generate meaningful revenue or achieve profitability will be materially and adversely affected.

In June 2025, we received FDA approval to commercialize IBTROZI in the U.S. for the treatment of adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic ROS1+ NSCLC, and we initiated a commercial launch of IBTROZI in the U.S. in that indication. IBTROZI is our only product approved for marketing by the FDA, and our ability to generate revenue from product sales and achieve profitability is mostly dependent on our ability to successfully commercialize IBTROZI in the U.S. We may not be able to successfully commercialize IBTROZI for a number of reasons, including:
• we may not be able to establish or demonstrate in the medical community the safety and efficacy of IBTROZI and its potential advantages over existing treatments;
• physicians may be reluctant to prescribe IBTROZI until longer-term efficacy and safety data exists;
• the length of time that patients who are prescribed IBTROZI remain on treatment may be shorter than we anticipate;

paragraphs: 2021 年 2 月 10 日（"成交日"），Nuvation Bio Inc.，一家特拉華州公司（"Legacy Nuvation Bio"），Panacea Acquisition Corp.（"Panacea"），以及 Panacea Merger Subsidiary Corp.，一家特拉華州公司且為 Panacea 直屬、 wholly owned 的子公司（"Merger Sub"），完成了於 2020 年 10 月 20 日簽訂之合併協議（"合併協議"）中所預期的交易。

根據合併協議的條款，Panacea 與 Legacy Nuvation Bio 進行了企業合併，透過 Merger Sub 與 Legacy Nuvation Bio 合併，且 Legacy Nuvation Bio 繼續作為 Panacea 的 wholly owned 子公司存續（"合併"）。在成交日，Legacy Nuvation Bio 改名為 Nuvation Bio Operating Company Inc.，Panacea 改名為 Nuvation Bio Inc.（"本公司" 或 "Nuvation Bio"）。
在合併交易完成後，本公司 A 普通股與購買 A 普通股權證於 2021 年 2 月 11 日開始在紐約證券交易所以符號 "NUVB" 與 "NUVB.WS" 進行交易。本報告第 1 與 1A 項之揭露已考量合併，並包含合併前 Legacy Nuvation Bio 之營運情形。

2024 年 4 月 9 日（"收購日"），本公司完成了對 AnHeart Therapeutics Ltd.，一家根據開曼羣島法律設立之豁免公司（"AnHeart"）之收購，根據該 Agreement and Plan of Merger（"AnHeart 合併協議"），由本公司、AnHeart、Artemis Merger Sub I, Ltd.，一家根據開曼羣島法律設立之豁免公司且為 wholly owned
本公司之子公司，以及Artemis Merger Sub II, Ltd.，為根據開曼羣島法律設立之豁免公司，為本公司之 wholly owned subsidiary。
"Nuvation Bio" 為 Nuvation Bio Inc. 在美國及其他國家註冊之商標。本報告中出現之其他商標或服務標誌，可能為其他所有者之商標或服務標誌。

本公司為一全球性腫瘤學公司，專注於解決癌症治療中的一些最困難挑戰，目標為開發能對患者生活產生深遠正面影響之療法。本公司於2018年由本公司首席執行長David Hung, M.D. 所創立，David Hung, M.D. 亦曾創立Medivation, Inc.，並領導其成功開發腫瘤學藥物Xtandi®與talazoparib（現已行銷為Talzenna®），導致其於2016年以14.3十億美元出售給Pfizer Inc.（"Pfizer"）。
我們運用團隊在藥物化學、臨牀前開發、藥物開發、商業發展、製造及商業化方面的廣泛專業知識，追蹤經強大臨牀或臨牀前數據驗證之腫瘤學目標，並開發新型小分子藥物，以提升現有市售藥物之療效並克服其缺點。
• 追尋已驗證的目標：我們識別並追尋經強力臨牀或前期臨牀數據驗證的腫瘤治療目標，這些目標能提供高度信心以產生臨牀意義的療效。我們專注於那些已有他人在臨牀候選藥物或核准藥物方面有所進展的目標，並試圖設計或取得創新或潛在最佳治療方案的產品候選藥物，以克服所遇到的安全性問題或療效限制。
• 創新的藥物化學專業知識：我們運用藥物化學專業知識，開發差異化的產品候選藥物，專注於提升其安全性、抗腫瘤活性及藥理特性，以超越其他標準治療（"SOC"）療法。我們也運用創新藥物化學方法，開發新類型的分子，例如我們的藥物-藥物-連結物（"DDCs"）。
• 人力資源管理：我們認為員工是我們最重要的資產。吸引、激勵並留住各層級人才對我們持續成功至關重要。我們正在建立一種文化，促進生產力、專業性與包容性的工作環境，讓員工能發揮所長、享受工作並受到啟發，以表現最佳表現。
以下表格總結我們的產品候選藥物開發管道：

我們於2025年6月在美國正式上市IBTROZI，其於2025年6月11日獲美國食品藥物管理局（"FDA"）核准，用於治療成人患有局部晚期或轉移性ROS1陽性（"ROS1+") 非小細胞肺癌（"NSCLC"）。Taletrectinib也已獲日本厚生勞動省（"MHLW"）及中國國家藥品監督管理局（"NMPA"）核准，用於治療成人患有ROS1+局部晚期或轉移性NSCLC（"mNSCLC"）。Taletrectinib在日本由我們的合作夥伴 nippon kayaku co., ltd ("NK") 以品牌名稱IBTROZI進行商業化，在中國由我們的合作夥伴 innovent biologics (suzhou) co., ltd. ("Innovent") 以品牌名稱DOVBLERON®進行商業化。Taletrectinib已獲美國FDA授予罕見疾病藥物指定（Orphan Drug Designation），用於治療ROS1+ NSCLC患者及其他NSCLC適應症，並曾獲美國FDA及中國NMPA授予突破性療法指定（Breakthrough Therapy Designations），用於治療局部晚期或轉移性ROS1+ NSCLC患者。2026年1月，我們宣佈與 Eisai Co., Ltd. ("Eisai") 籤訂合作夥伴關係，以在歐洲及其他美國、中國和日本以外的地區商業化taletrectinib。與Eisai合作，我們預計於2026年上半年向歐洲藥物管理局（"EMA"）提交市場許可申請（"MAA"）。

Taletrectinib持續評估用於治療局部晚期或轉移性ROS1+ NSCLC患者的兩項二期單臂關鍵性研究：TRUST-I於中國，以及TRUST-II，一項全球性研究，同時也在中國進行確認性隨機三期研究TRUST-III，對比crizotinib。2025年9月，我們宣佈首名患者已入組一項全球三期、安慰劑控制的研究TRUST-IV，用以評估taletrectinib用於切除ROS1+早期NSCLC患者的輔助治療。

paragraphs: 本公司業務及投資本公司證券涉及重大風險，部分風險已於下文說明。在您決定買進本公司證券前，除本報告書「警示財務預測陳述」節所討論的風險與不確定性外，您應謹慎考量下文所述的風險與不確定性，並配合本年度報告書第 10-K 表格所載的所有其他資訊，包括財務報表及其相關附註，以及「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析」節。如發生下文風險因素所述或本報告書其他地方所提及之事件或發展，將可能對本公司業務、財務狀況、營運成果、現金流、普通股交易價格及成長前景造成損害。尚有其他未為本公司所知或目前認為不重要之風險與不確定性，亦可能影響本公司業務營運。本第 10-K 表格報告書亦包含涉及風險與不確定性的財務預測陳述。本公司實際結果可能與財務預測陳述所預期者有重大差異，此乃因應下文風險因素及本報告書其他地方所提及之因素所致。
本公司近期前景嚴重依賴 IBTROZI 之商業化。若本公司無法成功商業化 IBTROZI，將對本公司產生重大且不利影響，使本公司無法產生有意義之營收或實現獲利。

2025 年 6 月，本公司獲得美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）核准，可在美國針對成人局部晚期或轉移性 ROS1+ 非小細胞肺癌（NSCLC）患者商業化 IBTROZI，並於該適應症於美國啟動 IBTROZI 之商業發行。IBTROZI 是本公司目前唯一經 FDA 批准上市之產品，本公司產生營收來自產品銷售及實現獲利之能力，主要取決於本公司能否成功於美國商業化 IBTROZI。本公司可能無法成功商業化 IBTROZI，原因包括：
• 本公司可能無法建立或證明 IBTROZI 在醫學界之安全性與有效性及其與現有治療之潛在優勢；
• 醫師可能在長期療效與安全性資料存在前，對開立 IBTROZI 有所保留；
• 被開立 IBTROZI 之患者持續接受治療之時間，可能短於本公司預期；
